# Implementing AI Algorithms from Scratch in C++ (Part 1): Comprehensive Learning Guide

## Course Overview

This advanced course bridges the gap between theoretical AI/ML concepts and their practical implementation in C++, one of the most demanding programming environments. You'll build foundational AI algorithms—including search strategies, decision trees, neural networks, and clustering methods—entirely from scratch, without relying on ML frameworks.

**Who it is for:**
- Software engineers preparing for FAANG interviews with AI/ML focus
- Systems programmers wanting to understand algorithm internals
- Competitive programmers seeking to deepen their DSA foundation
- Candidates targeting roles in quantitative finance, robotics, or autonomous systems

**Why it matters for interview prep:**
- Demonstrates deep algorithmic understanding beyond framework knowledge
- Shows mastery of memory management and performance optimization
- Reveals ability to debug complex numerical algorithms
- Proves proficiency with C++'s low-level abstractions (templates, pointers, SIMD)
- Competitive advantage: most candidates rely on scikit-learn or TensorFlow; you'll understand the mechanics

---

## Core Topics Covered

- **Graph-based Search Algorithms** – BFS, DFS, A*, Dijkstra's, and their application to pathfinding and game AI
- **Decision Trees & Ensemble Methods** – Building decision trees from scratch, implementing information gain calculations, and basic random forest logic
- **Linear Algebra for AI** – Matrix operations, eigenvalue decomposition, SVD, and their role in dimensionality reduction
- **Clustering Algorithms** – K-means, hierarchical clustering, DBSCAN, and centroid-based methods
- **Supervised Learning Foundations** – Linear regression, logistic regression, and gradient descent optimization
- **Unsupervised Learning & Dimensionality Reduction** – PCA, t-SNE, and autoencoders at a conceptual level
- **Neural Network Basics** – Perceptrons, backpropagation, fully-connected layers, and activation functions
- **Performance Optimization & Profiling** – Cache-aware data structures, SIMD usage, memory pooling, and algorithm benchmarking

---

## Learning Path Workflow

### Phase 1: Foundation & Setup (Tasks 1–8)
1. **C++ Project Setup** – Cmake configuration, dependency management (Eigen for linear algebra)
2. **Matrix & Vector Classes** – Build custom linear algebra structures; understand row-major vs. column-major layouts
3. **Basic Data Structures Review** – Graphs (adjacency list/matrix), heaps, hash tables optimized for AI workloads
4. **Algorithm Analysis Review** – Big O notation, space-time tradeoffs, cache complexity
5. **Numerical Stability Primer** – Floating-point precision, overflow/underflow, normalization techniques
6. **Testing & Benchmarking Framework** – Google Test setup, timing utilities, correctness validation
7. **Profiling Tools Introduction** – Valgrind, perf, gprof usage for algorithm profiling
8. **Hands-on: Implement a custom allocator** – Memory pool for matrix operations

### Phase 2: Graph-Based Search Algorithms (Tasks 9–18)
9. **BFS & DFS Implementation** – Build traversal algorithms on weighted/unweighted graphs
10. **Dijkstra's Algorithm** – Shortest path with custom priority queue
11. **A* Search Fundamentals** – Heuristics, open/closed sets, path reconstruction
12. **A* Implementation** – Full system for grid-based pathfinding (game AI context)
13. **Bidirectional Search** – Meet-in-the-middle optimization
14. **IDA* (Iterative Deepening A*)** – Memory-efficient variant
15. **Beam Search & Branch-and-Bound** – Approximate search methods
16. **Minimax with Alpha-Beta Pruning** – Game tree search
17. **Monte Carlo Tree Search (MCTS)** – Upper confidence bounds, rollout policies
18. **Benchmark Project: Maze Solver** – Compare all search methods on random mazes

### Phase 3: Linear Algebra & Mathematical Foundations (Tasks 19–28)
19. **Dense Matrix Multiplication** – Naive O(n³), cache-optimized, strassen algorithm
20. **QR Decomposition** – Gram-Schmidt orthogonalization
21. **Eigenvalue Decomposition (Power Iteration)** – For PCA and ranking
22. **Singular Value Decomposition (SVD)** – Low-rank approximations
23. **Matrix Inversion & Least Squares** – Pseudo-inverse, normal equations
24. **Vector Norms & Distance Metrics** – L1, L2, Cosine, Mahalanobis
25. **Numerical Stability in Linear Systems** – Condition numbers, regularization
26. **Sparse Matrix Operations** – CSR/COO formats for efficiency
27. **BLAS/SIMD Integration** – Vectorize matrix ops with SSE/AVX
28. **Project: PCA from Scratch** – Dimensionality reduction on real datasets

### Phase 4: Supervised Learning (Tasks 29–40)
29. **Linear Regression** – Normal equation and gradient descent derivation
30. **Gradient Descent Variants** – Batch, stochastic, mini-batch with momentum
31. **Feature Scaling & Normalization** – Standardization, min-max scaling
32. **Polynomial Features & Regularization** – Ridge (L2) and Lasso (L1) regression
33. **Logistic Regression** – Binary classification from first principles
34. **Softmax Regression** – Multi-class classification
35. **Decision Boundaries Visualization** – 2D plotting utilities
36. **Cross-Validation Framework** – K-fold, stratified splitting
37. **Model Evaluation Metrics** – Precision, recall, F1, ROC-AUC computation
38. **Hyperparameter Tuning** – Grid search, random search implementation
39. **Feature Selection Algorithms** – Backward elimination, forward selection
40. **Project: Iris/MNIST Classifier** – Binary and multi-class logistic regression

### Phase 5: Decision Trees & Ensemble Methods (Tasks 41–50)
41. **Information Theory Basics** – Entropy, information gain, gini impurity
42. **Decision Tree Node Class** – Recursive tree structure with split criteria
43. **Tree Building Algorithm** – ID3/C4.5-style recursive partitioning
44. **Handling Continuous & Categorical Features** – Binning, one-hot encoding
45. **Tree Pruning** – Cost-complexity pruning to prevent overfitting
46. **Random Forest Foundation** – Bootstrap sampling, feature subsets
47. **Random Forest Implementation** – Parallel tree training
48. **Gradient Boosting Basics** – Residual fitting concepts
49. **Feature Importance from Trees** – Gini/Information gain ranking
50. **Project: Titanic Survival Prediction** – Tree ensemble on structured data

### Phase 6: Clustering & Unsupervised Learning (Tasks 51–58)
51. **K-means Clustering** – Initialization strategies, convergence
52. **K-means++ Initialization** – Improved centroid selection
53. **Silhouette Score & Davies-Bouldin Index** – Cluster quality metrics
54. **Hierarchical Clustering** – Linkage methods (single, complete, average, Ward)
55. **Dendrogram Construction & Cutting** – Bottom-up clustering
56. **DBSCAN Algorithm** – Density-based clustering, epsilon-neighbors
57. **Elbow Method & Gap Statistic** – Optimal cluster detection
58. **Project: Customer Segmentation** – Clustering on high-dimensional retail data

### Phase 7: Neural Networks & Backpropagation (Tasks 59–65)
59. **Neuron & Activation Functions** – Sigmoid, ReLU, tanh implementations
60. **Forward Propagation** – Layer-by-layer computation
61. **Backpropagation Math** – Chain rule, gradient flow, weight updates
62. **Backpropagation Implementation** – Gradient computation for weights & biases
63. **Multi-layer Perceptron** – Arbitrary architecture support, initialization
64. **Batch Processing & Mini-batch GD** – Efficient training loops
65. **Project: MNIST Digit Recognition** – 2-3 layer network from scratch

---

## Key Skills You'll Build

### Algorithmic Mastery
- **Search Strategy Selection** – Understanding when to use BFS vs. A* vs. beam search
- **Optimization Dynamics** – Gradient-based optimization, convergence analysis, learning rate scheduling
